openings.claim: Opposed passive registration faces may replace strap tension as the lateral load carrier. The nearest rival is G0410’s strap-biased stops: slackening alignment tension should increase sliding there, but need not do so with passive capture.
openings.delta: Keep the paired padded strip shoes provisionally; arrange their exposed strip edges and two remaining bolts as opposed hatch-edge stops. Use straps only for local vertical retention, with cord retaining removable assemblies. This changes registration from tension-dependent seating to bounded geometric travel. Proceed only if measured geometry allows these faces using supplied stock.
openings.prediction: With vertical retention sufficient but alignment bias absent, the hatch remains within 1 mm under 20 N after ten openings, including the right-contact card disturbance; reopening remains within 30 seconds and the seal gains no visible tears. Shoe movement or loss of registration when bias is removed favors the rival. Performance is unknown.
openings.probe: Measure accessible underside purchase, stop height, opposed clearance and local strap reach first; missing purchase or faces ends this branch. Fabricate within ninety minutes. Use two setup closure/pull trials to compare bias present versus absent without removing vertical retention. Then ten numbered opening/closure/pull trials without bias, disturbing trial ten. Within twenty minutes record position, shoe movement, corner lift, reopening time and seal condition. More than 1 mm movement, shoe slip, obstruction, permanent deformation, a new tear or reopening over 30 seconds defeats the configuration; stop before damaging tightening. These observations test the replacement, not deployment.
assumptions: Underside access and shoe capacity remain unknown.
Supplied strips and bolts can establish opposed faces with less than 1 mm free travel despite the disturbed height.
Local straps can secure vertical retention; padding avoids deformation.
Fabrication and twelve trials fit stipulated time; removed assemblies clear the entire opening.

attacks.dependency: Strap bias seats the hatch against lateral stops.
Accessible rim underside provides adequate shoe purchase and capacity.

assessment: One uncertain opening preserves the outcome and constraints. Unknown geometry may prevent fabrication; a trial cap does not establish feasibility.

lineage.reason: Replace tension-dependent registration and explicitly test the retained underside-anchor dependency.
